# Robot Return to Origin.

@example Two moves right and two left cancel out, and so do the one up and the one down.
"RRULDL"
=> true

@example D and U take the robot back to (0, 0) early on, but R, R and L leave it at (1, 0).
"DURRL"
=> false

@example It ends at (-2, 2): as many moves up as to the left is not enough.
"UULL"
=> false

# A single move never comes back.
"U"
=> false

"D"
=> false

"L"
=> false

"R"
=> false

# Two opposite moves come back; two at right angles, or the same move
# twice, don't.
"DU"
=> true

"LR"
=> true

"UR"
=> false

"DD"
=> false

# As many moves right as down: one counter of +1 for U and R and -1 for D
# and L would read 0.
"RDDR"
=> false

# One move up against 2, 10, 256 or 1000 moves left, and one move down
# against 100 moves right: a single counter x + 2y, x + 10y, x + 256y,
# x + 1000y or x + 100y would read 0.
"ULL"
=> false

"ULLLLLLLLLL"
=> false

"ULLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLL"
=> false

""
=> false

"RRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRD"
=> false

# The same with the weight on the other axis: one move left or right
# against 2, 10, 100, 256 or 1000 moves up or down, so that a single
# counter 2x + y, 10x + y, 100x + y, 256x + y or 1000x + y would read 0.
"ULU"
=> false

"DDDDDRDDDDD"
=> false

"UUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUULUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUU"
=> false

"RDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDD"
=> false

""
=> false

# Ending at (2, -3) and at (3, -2): counters 3x + 2y and 2x + 3y read 0.
"DRDRD"
=> false

"RDRDR"
=> false

# A loop around a square, and a long excursion that comes back.
"URDL"
=> true

""
=> true

# Through (0, 0) four times, but one step away at the end.
"UDLRUDLRU"
=> false

# 256 moves more to the right than to the left, with the vertical moves
# balanced; then 256 moves up and none down. 8-bit counters would wrap.
""
=> false

"UUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUU"
=> false

# Each letter once, then one more: an odd number of moves never comes back.
"UDLRL"
=> false

# Random small cases from gen.c (lc check --regen makes them).
@gen 1 small
"RL"
=> true

@gen 2 small
"DLLU"
=> false

@gen 3 small
"UUDDURDDLDUU"
=> true

@gen 4 small
"DUDDUDUU"
=> true

@gen 5 small
"RLRLDLULRR"
=> true

@gen 6 small
"LUUURDUDDD"
=> true

@gen 7 small
"LURRURDRLL"
=> false

@gen 8 small
"DUL"
=> false
